Aholiab
ă-hō´lĭ-ăb
n. pr. m. (Hebrew 'Oholi'ab, tent of the father; the craftsman of Dan)
Hebrew 'ohel, tent, and 'ab, father — the father's tent. A fitting name for the man the LORD appointed to help build His.

Biblical Definition

Aholiab is Bezaleel's partner in building the tabernacle, and the LORD names him personally. “And I, behold, I have given with him Aholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan: and in the hearts of all that are wise hearted I have put wisdom, that they may make all that I have commanded thee” (Exo 31:6). He was gifted not only to work but to train others: “And he hath put in his heart that he may teach, both he, and Aholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan” (Exo 35:34). The work then proceeded: “Then wrought Bezaleel and Aholiab, and every wise hearted man, in whom the LORD put wisdom and understanding to know how to work all manner of work for the service of the sanctuary, according to all that the LORD had commanded” (Exo 36:1), and Moses summoned them: “And Moses called Bezaleel and Aholiab, and every wise hearted man, in whose heart the LORD had put wisdom, even every one whose heart stirred him up to come unto the work to do it” (Exo 36:2). His trades are listed at the close of the account: an engraver, and a cunning workman, and an embroiderer in blue, and in purple, and in scarlet, and fine linen (Exo 38:23).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) does not treat Scripture proper names; the sense is Hebrew, 'ohel, a tent, and 'ab, father — the father's tent.

expand to see more

AHOLIAB. A Hebrew proper name; from ohel, a tent, and ab, a father: the father's tent.

EMBROIDER, v.t. To border with ornamental needle-work, or figures.

CUNNING, a. Knowing; skilful; experienced; well-instructed. It is applied in Scripture to artificers, as a cunning workman.

Modern Corruption

Skilled work is treated as secular and only preaching as spiritual, while Exodus records the LORD naming two craftsmen and filling them with His Spirit for the job.

expand to see more

The first men in Scripture said to be filled with the Spirit of God are not prophets or priests but a jeweller and an embroiderer. Bezaleel of Judah and Aholiab of Dan — and the tribes matter, since Judah is the royal tribe and Dan the one that would give Israel its worst idolatry. The LORD named them both by name to Moses before either had cut a stone. Any doctrine of vocation that ranks the pulpit above the workbench has to explain Exodus 31.

Exodus 35:34 adds the detail most easily missed: God put it in his heart that he may teach. Aholiab was gifted to reproduce his skill in others, not merely to exercise it. A craftsman who trains no one has kept half his gift. The tabernacle was built by a workforce of wise hearted men whose competence came, the text says twice, from the LORD putting wisdom in their hearts — and two named men were charged with getting it into them.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew 'Oholi'ab (H171), tent of the father; 'ohel (H168), tent; chokmah (H2451), wisdom or skill; choshev, the cunning workman.

expand to see more

Hebrew 'Oholi'ab (H171) — Aholiab; Exodus 31:6, 35:34, 36:1, 38:23.

Hebrew 'ohel (H168) — tent; the first element, and the tabernacle itself.

Hebrew chokmah (H2451) — wisdom, skill; what the LORD put in the hearts of the workers.

Hebrew choshev (H2803) — cunning workman, deviser; one of Aholiab's trades.

Hebrew Dan (H1835) — Dan; his tribe, set beside royal Judah in the work.

Usage

"“I have given with him Aholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan” — named by the LORD."

"“He hath put in his heart that he may teach” — the gift includes reproducing it."

"“Every one whose heart stirred him up to come unto the work” — called, and willing."
